With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development […]]]></description><author>Justin Walker</author><guid isPermaLink="true">https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/rtx-spark-desktop-local-ai-available-now/</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:00:31 GMT</pubDate></item><item><title>NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout</title><link>https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-commitments-with-supply-chain-partners-to-support-ai-infrastructure-buildout</link><media:content url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/84535693a1e9e3e78bc4527fb059d368/6afcc4ea3d6332640221300a_nvidia-supply-chain-partners/nvidia-supply-chain-partners_thmb.jpg?v=0254b9a9-6c2c-455b-9cfa-df7b2323fa95" fileSize="166844" type="image/jpeg"></media:content><contentType>releases</contentType><image><img src="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/84535693a1e9e3e78bc4527fb059d368/6afcc4ea3d6332640221300a_nvidia-supply-chain-partners/nvidia-supply-chain-partners_thmb.jpg?v=0254b9a9-6c2c-455b-9cfa-df7b2323fa95" alt="NVIDIA Supply Chain Partners" align="left" hspace="15" vspace="5" /></image><subtitle>Long-Term Supply Agreements Across Multiple Critical Inputs Position NVIDIA for Sustainable Growth</subtitle><content><![CDATA[<p><strong>News Summary:</strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li>New agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics support additional substrate capacity and expanded production capabilities at existing factories.</li>
	<li>NVIDIA&rsquo;s work with Amkor and SPIL expands advanced packaging capacity for current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.</li>
	<li>NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in the third quarter, leveraging TSMC&rsquo;s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.</li>
	<li>Foxconn is deepening its collaboration with NVIDIA, drawing on its global production network to support next-generation GPU and networking platforms.</li>
</ul>

<p>NVIDIA today announced expanded commitments with supply chain partners to support sustainable long-term growth, aligning supply and manufacturing capacity with demand for its accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms.</p>

<p>Working with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, <a href="https://samsungsem.com/global/newsroom/news/overview.do" rel="" target="_blank" title="">Samsung Electro-Mechanics</a>, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and TSMC, NVIDIA is expanding manufacturing capacity across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer and contract manufacturing to scale production of its current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms.</p>

<p>&ldquo;Our supply chain is a strategic advantage,&rdquo; said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA. &ldquo;Our work with these partners builds on our manufacturing foundation for long-term growth, expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production to deliver the accelerated computing platforms our customers need.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Increasing Substrate Capacity and Production Capabilities</strong><br />
NVIDIA is expanding its substrate supply commitments with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, adding manufacturing capacity and improving production capabilities at existing factories.</p>

<p>Under a new agreement with NVIDIA, Kinsus plans to expand its advanced ABF package substrate manufacturing capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x over current levels from its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan.</p>

<p>Production is expected to begin in the second half of 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. This multiyear agreement builds on the companies&rsquo; existing supplier relationship and supports NVIDIA&rsquo;s long-term supply planning for its accelerated computing platforms.</p>

<p>&ldquo;We believe AI will be one of the most important technology transitions of our lifetime,&rdquo; said Scott Chen, CEO and president of Kinsus. &ldquo;After more than a decade of partnership with NVIDIA, we are excited to continue building the future together.&rdquo;</p>

<p>NVIDIA and Samsung Electro-Mechanics have amended their existing substrate supply agreement to improve operational capabilities at existing factories in support of increased production of NVIDIA&rsquo;s accelerated computing platforms.</p>

<p>The amendment builds on the companies&rsquo; <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>previously announced</u></a> multiyear&nbsp;collaboration supporting substrate manufacturing in Sejong and Busan, South Korea, for NVIDIA&rsquo;s compute and high-speed networking technologies.</p>

<p>&ldquo;By combining our world-class substrate fine-processing technology and high-reliability MLCC technology, we will perfectly fulfill our role as a total solution provider so that NVIDIA&rsquo;s AI platform can be supplied to the global market on time, with the highest performance and quality,&rdquo; said Duck-Hyun Chang, CEO of Samsung Electro-Mechanics.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p><strong>Scaling Advanced Packaging Through Multiyear Agreements</strong><br />
NVIDIA&rsquo;s advanced packaging plans include a new capacity expansion with SPIL and previously announced agreements supporting Amkor&rsquo;s manufacturing expansion in the U.S. and South Korea.</p>

<p>NVIDIA is supporting Amkor&rsquo;s expansion of advanced packaging capacity in Arizona and South Korea through multiyear agreements announced in <a href="https://ir.amkor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amkor-technology-announces-strategic-partnership-nvidia-expand" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>July</u></a> and <a href="https://ir.amkor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amkor-technology-and-nvidia-advance-strategic-partnership-ai" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>October</u></a> 2026, totaling nearly $3 billion. The agreements include prepayments to help Amkor scale manufacturing capacity for NVIDIA&rsquo;s long-term production needs.</p>

<p>&ldquo;Our agreements with NVIDIA support investments in Arizona and South Korea that will serve multiple generations of AI platforms,&rdquo; said Kevin Engel, president and CEO of Amkor. &ldquo;That long-term planning allows us to advance our packaging technologies and add manufacturing capacity as NVIDIA&rsquo;s production needs grow.&rdquo;</p>

<p>NVIDIA and SPIL are expanding advanced packaging operations in Taiwan under a multiyear agreement supported by multibillion-dollar funding from NVIDIA. The expansion will increase contracted advanced packaging capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by mid-2029.</p>

<p>The project includes new production lines with turnkey support spanning bumping, interposer wafer fabrication, assembly and testing. These capabilities support semiconductor products with demanding requirements for computing performance, bandwidth, power efficiency and system integration.</p>

<p>&ldquo;SPIL is proud to strengthen our collaboration with NVIDIA,&rdquo; said C.W. Tsai, CEO and chairman of the board of SPIL. &ldquo;This agreement enhances our ability to support next‑generation packaging technologies and deliver the performance and reliability required for future AI systems.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Next-Generation Technologies for Agentic AI</strong><br />
The third quarter marked the first volume shipment of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs for agentic AI. These products take advantage of TSMC&rsquo;s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.</p>

<p>&ldquo;TSMC and NVIDIA share a longstanding partnership built on semiconductor innovation,&rdquo; said Dr. Kevin Zhang, senior vice president and deputy co-COO at TSMC. &ldquo;This deep collaboration allows us to plan for future technology requirements and prepare our manufacturing capabilities as NVIDIA brings new platforms to market.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Leveraging Global Manufacturing Footprint for GPU and Networking Platforms</strong><br />
&ldquo;Foxconn continues to deepen its collaboration with NVIDIA across next-generation GPU and networking platforms,&rdquo; said Young Liu, chairman of Foxconn. &ldquo;By leveraging its integrated global production network spanning Asia, North America, and Europe, Foxconn is well-positioned to support the volume ramp-up of next-generation AI infrastructure.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Building on Global Supply Chain Expansion</strong><br />
These commitments build on NVIDIA&rsquo;s decades-long partnerships and recent commitments announced in <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>October</u></a> for manufacturing expansions with Amkor, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL and Unimicron. Those plans included an aggregate 2.5x increase in substrate capacity over three years, expanded advanced packaging, a doubling of semiconductor testing capacity from 2026 to 2027 and a 15x increase in SPIL&rsquo;s optical-engine capacity by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.</p>

<p>&ldquo;Our strong and long-standing collaboration with NVIDIA has continued to develop in the area of high-performance IC package substrates,&rdquo; said Koji Kawashima, president and chief executive officer at IBIDEN. &ldquo;Through the expansion of our Ono Plant, we will continue to strengthen our production capabilities and meet growing demand.&rdquo;</p>

<p>&ldquo;Our work with NVIDIA demonstrates the value of close collaboration between chip design and semiconductor testing,&rdquo; said Gauss Chang, president at KYEC. &ldquo;Expanding our testing operations into the United States builds on that relationship and brings our capabilities closer to NVIDIA&rsquo;s growing U.S. manufacturing supply chain.&rdquo;</p>

<p>&ldquo;As AI reshapes industries and societies around the world, trusted partnerships and supply chain collaboration have never been more important,&rdquo; said SC Chien, chairman of Unimicron. &ldquo;The advanced substrate capacity investment underscores the strength of our partnership with NVIDIA and our shared commitment to support the rapid growth of AI infrastructure. <p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively.&nbsp;</p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">&ldquo;Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,&rdquo; said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. &ldquo;Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.&rdquo;</p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">In September 2026, NVIDIA&rsquo;s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company&rsquo;s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization.</p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026.</p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;"><strong>Outlook</strong></p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">NVIDIA&rsquo;s outlook for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, which includes an additional week, is as follows:</p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Revenue is expected to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $11.0 billion and $10.7 billion, respectively.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">For the full year fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to be between 16.0% and 18.0%, excluding any discrete items and material changes to NVIDIA&rsquo;s tax environment.</li>
</ul>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;"><strong>Highlights</strong></p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;"><strong>Data Center </strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Third-quarter revenue was $107.6 billion, up 21% from the previous quarter and up 110% from a year ago.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Ramped production and began shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 &mdash; the fastest product ramp in the company&rsquo;s history &mdash; with racks <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/vera-rubin/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="running">running</a> at partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius, and coming online soon at SpaceXSI.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded the Vera Rubin cloud ecosystem, announcing general availability of Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs on <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-oracle-expand-nvidia-vera-rubin-to-multi-gigawatt-scale-and-bring-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-oracle-cloud-infrastructure" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Oracle Cloud Infrastructure">Oracle Cloud Infrastructure</a>, general availability of <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/google-cloud-vera-rubin-infrastructure/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Google Cloud’s">Google Cloud&rsquo;s</a> Vera Rubin-powered A5X instances and the continued buildout of SpaceXSI&rsquo;s infrastructure.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ocp-global-summit-vera-rubin-scale-ai-factories/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Vera Rubin">Vera Rubin</a> open architecture advances to help the industry scale faster, and revealed that Cisco, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Visionbay are joining many technology leaders advancing infrastructure for Vera Rubin.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Revealed that leading AI natives, cloud providers and neoclouds, including CoreWeave, Meta, Nebius, Nscale, OpenAI and Verda, are building with <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/european-leaders-vera-cpu-infrastructure/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Vera CPUs">NVIDIA Vera CPUs</a> to support the growing computing needs of businesses and developers, joining AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and SpaceXSI.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded Anthropic&rsquo;s access to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers, and continued to collaborate on design and engineering to optimize future NVIDIA architectures for Anthropic&rsquo;s workloads.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced the <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-vera-cpu-platform-to-accelerate-scientific-discovery" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Vera CPU">NVIDIA Vera CPU</a> rack-scale platform for high-performance computing &mdash; combining NVIDIA&rsquo;s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Introduced <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/rubin-hpc/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Rubin HPC">NVIDIA Rubin HPC</a>, a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows.&nbsp;</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded collaboration with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-meta-to-expand-collaboration-on-muse-and-muse-family-of-models-amid-robust-growth" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Meta">Meta</a> on AI agent Muse and its family of models, with Meta planning expanded deployment of Vera Rubin, Vera CPUs, NVIDIA Spectrum-X&trade; networking and NVIDIA BlueField<sup>&reg;</sup>-4 to scale training, inference and agents.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Introduced <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-dsx-pod-ai-factories-to-accelerate-europes-infrastructure-deployment" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="DSX POD">DSX POD</a>, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery to accelerate infrastructure deployment.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced European ecosystem adoption of <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-ecosystem-builds-worlds-most-efficient-ai-factories-with-nvidia-dsx" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA DSX">NVIDIA DSX</a>&trade; to reduce AI factory power requirements and enable near-zero facility cooling water consumption.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced that NVIDIA swept every <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/mlperf-training-endpoints-vera-rubin/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="MLPerf Training and Endpoints">MLPerf Training and Endpoints</a> benchmark, and Vera Rubin NVL72 demonstrated leading inference performance in its <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/vera-rubin-nvl72-mlperf-inference/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="MLPerf Inference">MLPerf Inference</a> preview debut.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Launched <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/open-agent-safety-platform" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform">NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform</a> and introduced the <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/openshell-reference-architecture" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture">NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture</a>, combining open source OpenShell software, Vera Rubin for model inference, Vera CPUs for agent execution and BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry to independently monitor agent behavior and enforce security policies in silicon.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced an agreement to acquire <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-to-acquire-hugging-face/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Hugging Face">Hugging Face</a> to scale its platform and make intelligence more open, capable and accessible.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced plans with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="global supply chain partners">global supply chain partners</a>, including <a href="https://ir.amkor.com/news-releases/news-release-details/amkor-technology-and-nvidia-advance-strategic-partnership-ai" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Amkor Technology">Amkor Technology</a>, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics, <a href="https://samsungsem.com/global/newsroom/news/view.do?id=10614" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Samsung Electro-Mechanics">Samsung Electro-Mechanics</a>, <a href="https://www.spilglobal.com/NewsDetail/d968ea095a2d08fe" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Siliconware Precision Industries">Siliconware Precision Industries</a> and Unimicron Technology Corporation, to scale critical manufacturing capabilities to meet demand for NVIDIA infrastructure.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Deepened partnership with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-mediatek-deepen-long-standing-partnership-to-build-ai-edge-to-cloud-computing-platforms" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="MediaTek">MediaTek</a> across cloud infrastructure, local computing and automotive, extending NVIDIA&rsquo;s rack-scale platform to custom XPUs through NVIDIA NVLink Fusion&trade;.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced plans with Cisco for <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-cisco-introduce-new-pluggable-optics-form-factor-to-scale-ai-factories" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="USFP">USFP</a>, a new optical-module form factor designed to increase bandwidth density and power efficiency for next-generation AI factory networks.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced collaboration with Australia&rsquo;s data center ecosystem on infrastructure supporting a planned buildout of up to 2 gigawatts by 2027 for <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-ai-infrastructure-capacity-in-partnership-with-australias-data-center-ecosystem" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA DSX">NVIDIA DSX</a> AI factories.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Introduced <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-nemotron-for-science-to-accelerate-discoveries-with-agents" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Nemotron for Science">NVIDIA Nemotron for Science</a> to help researchers build specialized agents for scientific discovery, and collaborated with global <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/healthcare-and-life-sciences-leaders-build-on-nvidia-to-advance-drug-discovery-and-expand-patient-care" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="healthcare and life sciences organizations">healthcare and life sciences organizations</a> to advance protein design, accelerate drug discovery and expand precision patient care.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Partnered with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-palantir-bring-sovereign-intelligence-to-critical-supply-chains" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Palantir">Palantir</a> to bring sovereign AI intelligence and NVIDIA Nemotron&trade; open models to critical supply chains.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Partnered with <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/kazakhstan-ai-compute-ecosystem/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Firebird">Firebird</a> to scale the company&rsquo;s total potential AI infrastructure capacity.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded the open source NVIDIA CUDA-Q&trade; platform with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-open-source-cuda-q-platform-for-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="CUDA-Q Logical">CUDA-Q Logical</a> for fault-tolerant quantum computing development, and ran a <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-runs-record-simulation-of-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing-at-julich-supercomputing-centre" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="record simulation">record simulation</a> of a fault-tolerant quantum processor on JUPITER at the J&uuml;lich Supercomputing Centre.</li>
</ul>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;"><strong>Edge Computing</strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Third-quarter Edge Computing revenue was $8.2 billion, up 14% from the previous quarter and up 42% from a year ago.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Reinvented Windows PCs with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-rtx-spark-pcs-available-today-a-new-beginning-for-windows-pcs" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA RTX Spark™">NVIDIA RTX Spark&trade;</a> laptops, now shipping from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface and MSI.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Launched NVIDIA DLSS 5 in <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/dlss-5-3d-guided-neural-rendering/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em>NBA 2K27</em></a> and <em>Hogwarts Legacy</em>, bringing AI-powered, photorealistic lighting and materials to GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, GeForce NOW and RTX Spark, and coming soon to <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/hogwarts-legacy-war-thunder-dlss-5-3d-guided-neural-rendering/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em>Where Winds Meet</em></a>.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded the NVIDIA local AI lineup with a new <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/local-ai-dgx-spark-64gb-sync/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA DGX Spark™">NVIDIA DGX Spark&trade;</a> 64GB model, bringing near-frontier AI capabilities to desktops at a more accessible price point, and accelerated <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/local-ai-rtx-spark-laptops-updates-models-agents-games/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="leading AI models">leading AI models</a> from NVIDIA Nemotron, Black Forest Labs, Liquid AI and Qwen for running AI agents locally, with <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/local-ai-ifa-next-gen-agents-nv-pair-rtx-spark/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="expanded support">expanded support</a> for Hermes, OpenClaw and Perplexity.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Introduced new NVIDIA Alpamayo&trade; development tools and the <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-mobility-leaders-build-safe-vehicles-and-robotaxi-fleets-on-nvidia-hyperion" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Halos™ SAFE">NVIDIA Halos&trade; SAFE</a> framework to help developers build and evaluate autonomous-driving systems.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded partnerships with <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/mercedes-benz-and-nvidia-expand-strategic-partnership-to-advance-safe-highly-automated-driving-in-the-next-decade" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Mercedes-Benz">Mercedes-Benz</a> and <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/volvo-cars-and-nvidia-expand-partnership-to-advance-safe-automated-driving" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Volvo Cars">Volvo Cars</a> to advance safe automated driving.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Announced European mobility leaders &mdash; including Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride &mdash; are showcasing <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/european-mobility-leaders-build-safe-vehicles-and-robotaxi-fleets-on-nvidia-hyperion" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Hyperion">NVIDIA Hyperion</a>&trade; use cases for automated vehicles and future robotaxi fleets.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Advanced the <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-advances-isaac-platform-for-general-purpose-robotics-with-new-reference-humanoid-frameworks-simulation-pipelines-and-data" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Isaac">NVIDIA Isaac</a>&trade; robotics platform with new development tools, datasets and runtime, alongside Agile Robots&rsquo; introduction of a reference humanoid powered by NVIDIA Jetson Thor&trade; and built on Isaac GR00T.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Expanded <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/cosmos-open-train-evaluate-deploy-world-models/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Cosmos">NVIDIA Cosmos</a>&trade; with tools to train, evaluate and deploy world models for robotics, autonomous vehicles and industrial applications.</li>
	<li style="margin-bottom:9pt; text-align:justify;">Advanced <a href="https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-nokia-and-leading-telecom-operators-turn-networks-into-distributed-intelligence-platforms" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="AI-RAN">AI-RAN</a> with Nokia and global telecom operators, including T-Mobile&rsquo;s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, bringing NVIDIA accelerated computing deeper into wireless networks.</li>
</ul>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;"><strong>Non-GAAP Measures</strong></p>

<p align="justify" style="text-align:justify;">To supplement NVIDIA&rsquo;s condensed consolidated financial statements presented in accordance with GAAP, the company uses non-GAAP measures of certain components of financial performance. These non-GAAP measures include non-GAAP gross profit, non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP other income (expense), net, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP net income, or earnings, per diluted share, and free cash flow. For NVIDIA&rsquo;s investors to be better able to compare its current results with those of previous periods, the company has shown a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial measures. These reconciliations adjust the related GAAP financial measures to exclude acquisition-related and other costs, other, legal settlement costs, gains/losses from equity securities, net, certain other income and expense, and the associated tax impact of these items where applicable. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA&rsquo;s non-GAAP financial measures no longer exclude stock-based compensation expense. The historical non-GAAP financial information presented has been updated to include stock-based compensation expense. Free cash flow is calculated as GAAP net cash provided by operating activities less both purchases related to property and equipment and intangible assets and principal payments on property and equipment and intangible assets. NVIDIA believes the presentation of its non-GAAP financial measures enhances the users&rsquo; overall understanding of the company&rsquo;s historical financial performance. The presentation of the company&rsquo;s non-GAAP financial measures is not meant to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the company&rsquo;s financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP, and the company&rsquo;s non-GAAP measures may be different from non-GAAP measures used by other companies.</p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li>Committee to provide oversight over NVIDIA&rsquo;s national security and global trade compliance programs</li>
	<li>Committee will retain independent, outside experts to provide legal, national security and trade compliance expertise to support the Committee</li>
	<li>Director Suzanne Nora Johnson appointed Committee Chair</li>
</ul>

<p>NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that the Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, a new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company&rsquo;s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management. NVIDIA&rsquo;s existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the Committee and to Interim CEO, Colette Kress, on day-to-day operations.</p>

<p>The Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will also include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive session. The Committee will oversee the Company&rsquo;s ongoing efforts to enhance its internal National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team, and work closely with independent third-party experts in law, national security and global trade compliance.</p>

<p>&ldquo;NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security. As the world&rsquo;s leading advanced computing company, NVIDIA has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that&nbsp;uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard&nbsp;national security while supporting continued technological innovation,&rdquo; said Harvey Jones, Chairman of NVIDIA&rsquo;s Board of Directors.</p>

<p>The decision to create this new committee reflects the Board&rsquo;s further commitment to enhance its engagement with relevant government stakeholders, and to demonstrate the highest standards of governance and oversight.</p>

Advance Practical Quantum Computing</title><link>https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-collaboration-with-ibm-and-fermi-national-accelerator-laboratory-to-launch-quantum-classical-codesign-platform-plus-error-correction-breakthrough-to-advance-practical-quantum-computing</link><media:content url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/40e6822d3e59526b227f38a356e88502/6af958f13d6332343c233577_ibm-nvidia-fermilab/ibm-nvidia-fermilab_thmb.jpg?v=013b8ce3-bbf0-4795-a9b5-284c46b0f175" alt="IBM, NVIDIA and Fermilab" align="left" hspace="15" vspace="5" /></image><subtitle>IBM and NVIDIA Work With Fermilab in Developing Modular Architectures for Scalable Quantum Computers — Separately, Breakthrough NVIDIA CUDA-Q Algorithm Delivers up to 13,000x Faster Decoding for Error-Correction Research</subtitle><content><![CDATA[<p><strong>News Summary:</strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li>NVIDIA and IBM announce a growing quantum supercomputing collaboration combining NVIDIA accelerated computing and software with IBM quantum computers to advance quantum error-correction research, scientific applications and integration into supercomputing workflows. NVIDIA DGX B200 systems will connect with IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful processor IBM has yet built.</li>
	<li>A quantum computing codesign platform with Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, alongside IBM and NVIDIA, will support quantum error-correction and applications research for future systems.</li>
	<li>NVIDIA releases TCBP-JOBS, a new decoding algorithm part of the CUDA-Q platform, that delivers up to a 13,000x speedup for quantum error-correction research, accelerating fault-tolerant quantum computation.</li>
	<li>NVIDIA is expanding Slurm to simplify scheduling quantum processors within supercomputing workflows, with IBM contributing integration through its Quantum Resource Management Interface.</li>
</ul>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">NVIDIA today announced plans for new collaborations with <a href="https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-11-16-ibm,-fermilab,-and-nvidia-announce-plans-for-new-co-design-platform-to-accelerate-the-development-of-next-generation,-modular-quantum-computers" rel="" target="_blank" title="">IBM</a> and the <a href="https://news.fnal.gov/2026/11/fermilab-ibm-and-nvidia-plan-modular-quantum-computing-co-design-platform-to-advance-scientific-discovery/" rel="" target="_blank" title="">U.S. Department of Energy&rsquo;s Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory</a> that will span research into next-generation modular architectures for quantum computers, scientific applications and supercomputing integration. These efforts, including a new modular quantum computing codesign platform with IBM and Fermilab, combine NVIDIA accelerated computing and software with IBM quantum computers to help researchers scale quantum computers and explore their scientific capabilities.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">Separately, NVIDIA also announced a new quantum algorithm that delivers up to 13,000x faster decoding compared with existing leading algorithms &mdash; cutting the computation time for researching new quantum computing designs from 12 weeks to just 45 minutes.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">The collaboration with IBM also brings together new Slurm capabilities integrations to simplify how quantum computers can be added into supercomputing workflows.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;"><strong>Modular Quantum Computing Codesign Platform</strong><br />
IBM and NVIDIA are colocating NVIDIA DGX&trade; B200 systems with state-of-the-art IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the fastest quantum processor IBM has ever delivered. This integrated system is supporting a jointly developed IBM, Fermilab and NVIDIA modular quantum codesign platform.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">The codesign platform will allow researchers to develop and evaluate error-correction codes, decoding algorithms and quantum-classical applications driving scientific discoveries in high-energy and nuclear physics (HENP), as well as how classical systems can scale alongside multiple linked quantum processors within modular architectures.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">Fermilab&rsquo;s expertise will allow work at the platform to focus on quantum error correction and HENP applications &mdash; helping define requirements for future fault-tolerant quantum computers and the science that can be achieved with them.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">&ldquo;Making quantum computers useful for science requires advances in error correction, applications and the systems that bring quantum processors and accelerated computing together,&rdquo; said Krysta Svore, vice president of applied research for quantum computing at NVIDIA. &ldquo;NVIDIA&rsquo;s research software and our collaboration with IBM give scientists more powerful tools to investigate quantum designs and develop applications across these systems.&rdquo;</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">&ldquo;Some of the most fundamental problems in science remain out of reach without access to quantum computing. Scaling quantum and classical together will open new frontiers in high-energy and nuclear physics and beyond,&rdquo; said Jerry Chow, IBM Fellow and chief technology officer of quantum-centric computing. &ldquo;With Fermilab and NVIDIA, we plan to explore how these real-world problems can help us shape the modular, interconnected architectures that will define the next generation of quantum computers and accelerated classical computing.&rdquo;</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">&ldquo;The future of quantum computing depends on more than advances in quantum hardware alone,&rdquo; said Anna Grassellino, Fermilab chief technology officer and director of the SQMS Center. &ldquo;Accelerated computing and superintelligence will play an important role in how we design algorithms, study errors and coordinate increasingly complex quantum systems. This proposed platform would combine NVIDIA&rsquo;s computing capabilities with IBM&rsquo;s quantum technologies and Fermilab&rsquo;s scientific expertise, and would enable researchers to explore new approaches to codesigning quantum computers that meet the needs of challenging HENP science problems.&rdquo;</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;"><strong>Advancing Quantum Error-Correction Research</strong><br />
Errors inherent to quantum processors limit the complexity and duration of the computations they can perform. Quantum error correction protects quantum information by encoding it across multiple physical qubits. A classical algorithm called a decoder interprets measurement data to identify likely errors so they can be corrected.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">Available through the NVIDIA CUDA-Q&trade; QEC 0.9.0 library today, <a href="https://research.nvidia.com/publication/_tcbpjobs-gpu-accelerated-quantum-error-correction-decoding-and-noise-learning-near" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA’s new TCBP-JOBS decoding algorithm">NVIDIA&rsquo;s new TCBP-JOBS decoding algorithm</a> accelerates the computationally intensive parts of quantum error-correction research by up to 13,000x while delivering high accuracy. Faster decoding in research workloads allows scientists to evaluate candidate error-correction approaches more efficiently and explore how different codes and decoder configurations perform.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">The new decoding algorithm provides researchers with tools to identify designs that use physical qubits more efficiently, and better measure their performance improvements, shortening the path to practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.</p>

<p><strong>Advancing Quantum Chemistry&nbsp;</strong><br />
IBM and RIKEN are advancing quantum-classical chemistry research powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. The work, which combines IBM&rsquo;s quantum computer with RIKEN&rsquo;s JHPC-quantum GPU supercomputer ROQUO, has been named a finalist for the 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize.</p>

<p>The researchers calculated binding energies for two protein-ligand complexes to study interactions relevant to drug discovery. By dividing the systems into fragments and combining quantum sampling with GPU-accelerated calculations, they modeled complexes containing up to 12,635 atoms &mdash; more than 40x the size of the previous 303-atom quantum-classical benchmark.&nbsp;</p>

<p>ROQUO uses NVIDIA GB200 systems and NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking to support research in quantum algorithms, simulation and hybrid computing.</p>

<p>This research is supported by NEDO (New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization), an organization under the jurisdiction of Japan&rsquo;s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry&rsquo;s &ldquo;Research and Development of Quantum-Supercomputers Hybrid Platform for Exploration of Uncharted Computable Capabilities.&rdquo;</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;"><strong>Bringing Quantum Into Supercomputing Workflows</strong><br />
NVIDIA is expanding the open source Slurm workload manager with a quantum interface that simplifies integrating quantum processors into supercomputing environments. IBM is contributing to the integration through its Quantum Resource Management Interface, connecting IBM quantum resources to the new Slurm capabilities.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">Supercomputing centers rely on a variety of custom approaches to integrate quantum hardware, creating additional engineering and maintenance work as centers add quantum processors and develop hybrid applications.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;">The <a href="https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/slurm-quantum-computing-supercomputing" rel="" target="_blank" title=""><u>new Slurm capabilities</u></a> will allow centers and researchers to schedule quantum processors alongside CPUs and GPUs using familiar commands, policies and tools.</p>

<p align="left" style="text-align:left;"><em>Learn more about </em><a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/solutions/quantum-computing/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em><u>NVIDIA technologies for quantum computing</u></em></a><em>.</em></p>
]]></content><categories><category>Press Releases</category></categories><modDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:15:21 GMT</modDate><relatedPages></relatedPages><description><![CDATA[NVIDIA today announced plans for new collaborations with IBM and the U.S. Department of Energy’s Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory that will span research into next-generation modular architectures for quantum computers, scientific applications and supercomputing integration.]]></description><enclosure url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/40e6822d3e59526b227f38a356e88502/ibm-nvidia-fermilab.jpeg" length="1084001" type="image/jpeg"></enclosure><guid isPermaLink="true">https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-collaboration-with-ibm-and-fermi-national-accelerator-laboratory-to-launch-quantum-classical-codesign-platform-plus-error-correction-breakthrough-to-advance-practical-quantum-computing</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:00:00 GMT</pubDate></item><item><title>NVIDIA Expands Vera CPU Platform to Accelerate Scientific Discovery</title><link>https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-vera-cpu-platform-to-accelerate-scientific-discovery</link><media:content url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/52681341f671bc3c34a4329aa393c846/6af8c0083d63329aad233567_nvidia-vera-rack/nvidia-vera-rack_thmb.jpg?v=d8e83da7-e05d-4c1b-9368-96ce3fa2392e" fileSize="60430" type="image/jpeg"></media:content><contentType>releases</contentType><image><img src="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/52681341f671bc3c34a4329aa393c846/6af8c0083d63329aad233567_nvidia-vera-rack/nvidia-vera-rack_thmb.jpg?v=d8e83da7-e05d-4c1b-9368-96ce3fa2392e" alt="NVIDIA Vera CPU Platform" align="left" hspace="15" vspace="5" /></image><subtitle>Vera Delivers Higher Performance for Agentic Science and 2x Greater Energy Efficiency Than x86 CPUs</subtitle><content><![CDATA[<p><strong>News Summary:</strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li>The NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform combines NVIDIA processors, NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking and breakthrough scientific software to boost weather, climate and molecular simulations.</li>
	<li>DKRZ has selected Vera CPUs for its HLRE-5 supercomputer for climate science.</li>
	<li>The full Vera CPU platform is coming from Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro.</li>
</ul>

<p>NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing &mdash; combining NVIDIA&rsquo;s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for state-of-the-art scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science.</p>

<p>The rack-scale platform brings together 192 <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-cpu/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="Vera CPUs">Vera CPUs</a> interconnected by <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/networking/products/infiniband/quantum-x800/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand">NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand</a> networking to meet the massive performance demands of climate modeling, molecular dynamics and other unaccelerated, next-generation scientific workloads.</p>

<p>The liquid-cooled system delivers more than 200TB/s of aggregate peak memory bandwidth to support scientific simulation and AI workflows.</p>

<p>&ldquo;Scientific simulations need CPUs that can keep large datasets moving and sustain performance as applications scale,&rdquo; said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. &ldquo;Vera brings custom CPU cores, high-bandwidth memory and InfiniBand networking together to address those bottlenecks. With compilers and libraries optimized for Vera, researchers can run demanding simulations more efficiently and explore more complex scientific problems.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Engineered for Memory-Intensive HPC</strong><br />
Each Vera CPU features 88 custom NVIDIA Olympus cores, 176 threads and compact, serviceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X memory delivering up to 1.2TB/s of bandwidth to accelerate data-intensive scientific applications.</p>

<p>The rack combines 192 Vera CPUs with approximately 300TB of memory and 1 petabyte of storage in a fully liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX&trade; design. Each 1U tray integrates eight Vera CPUs, and NVMe storage and management.</p>

<p>The platform reuses NVL72 rack components, including chassis, power distribution and cooling infrastructure, to simplify deployment and service. NVIDIA Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking connects the system, and NVIDIA SHARP&trade; In-Network Computing helps scientists finish complex simulations faster by reducing the time processors spend coordinating their work.</p>

<p>In NVIDIA&rsquo;s tests, Vera delivered 1.9x the performance and 2.4x the performance per watt of x86 systems on OpenFOAM&rsquo;s motorBike Large airflow simulation.</p>

<p><strong>Advancing Climate Science Research</strong><br />
NVIDIA has benchmarked the open source Weather Research and Forecasting model on Vera CPUs, with projected performance gains of 1.6x and energy-efficiency gains of 2x compared with x86.</p>

<p>DKRZ, the German Climate Computing Center, has selected Vera CPUs for its HLRE-5 supercomputer, alongside NVIDIA GB200 Grace Blackwell systems and NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking. Built by Bull and expected to be available in early 2028, the system will support climate simulation and AI research, enabling global kilometer-scale climate simulations with lower energy consumption than on the current system.</p>

<p><strong>Software and Availability</strong><br />
To help researchers speed scientific applications, <a href="https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title="NVIDIA HPC SDK 26.11">NVIDIA HPC SDK 26.11</a> is available now, providing compilers and libraries optimized for Vera.</p>

<p>NVIDIA is also introducing a public beta of its next-generation Fortran compiler, which was built in collaboration with leading HPC centers and national labs. The new compiler gives developers a way to run their existing programs built on Fortran &mdash; the language that scientific computing was built on &mdash; with greater speed on NVIDIA platforms, without needing to rewrite their code.</p>

<p>Vera CPU racks are expected to be available from Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro beginning in early 2027.</p>

<p><em>Learn more about the </em><a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/vera-cpu/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em>NVIDIA Vera CPU</em></a><em>. For detailed benchmark results and test configurations, read the </em><a href="https://dam-cdn.nvd.orangelogic.com/AssetLink/b8ip35u047q24s1600wns7rtilf0qcru.pdf" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em>NVIDIA Vera CPU HPC performance brief</em></a><em>.</em></p>
]]></content><categories><category>Press Releases</category></categories><modDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:06:56 GMT</modDate><relatedPages></relatedPages><description><![CDATA[NVIDIA today announced the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack-scale platform for high-performance computing — combining NVIDIA’s first fully custom data center CPU with the gold standard for HPC networking to drive extreme efficiency and throughput for state-of-the-art scientific modeling, simulation and agentic science.]]></description><enclosure url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/52681341f671bc3c34a4329aa393c846/nvidia-vera-rack.jpg" length="60430" type="image/jpeg"></enclosure><guid isPermaLink="true">https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-expands-vera-cpu-platform-to-accelerate-scientific-discovery</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:00:00 GMT</pubDate></item><item><title>NVIDIA Introduces Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Discoveries With Agents</title><link>https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-nemotron-for-science-to-accelerate-discoveries-with-agents</link><media:content url="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/bbee83cc9133eb5438c52eab3fd409e2/6af8bac03d6332a556233545_nvidia-nemotron-for-science/nvidia-nemotron-for-science_thmb.jpg?v=3ae01a42-fd11-4792-b9a1-a25649fd94c1" fileSize="942357" type="image/jpeg"></media:content><contentType>releases</contentType><image><img src="https://iprsoftwaremedia.com/219/files/202611/bbee83cc9133eb5438c52eab3fd409e2/6af8bac03d6332a556233545_nvidia-nemotron-for-science/nvidia-nemotron-for-science_thmb.jpg?v=3ae01a42-fd11-4792-b9a1-a25649fd94c1" alt="NVIDIA Nemotron for Science" align="left" hspace="15" vspace="5" /></image><subtitle>New Open Dataset and Post-Training Recipes Help Researchers Adapt Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for Life Sciences and Chemistry</subtitle><content><![CDATA[<p><strong>News Summary:</strong></p>

<ul type="disc">
	<li>NVIDIA Nemotron for Science brings together the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model, scientific evaluations, a new open chemistry dataset and recipes to help researchers build domain-specific science agents.</li>
	<li>LitmusBench v0.2 supports both evaluation and post-training for chemistry reasoning, helping researchers assess model capabilities and adapt models to scientific tasks.</li>
	<li>NVIDIA DGX Spark and data center infrastructure take Nemotron 3.5 Super VL from researchers&rsquo; desktops to supercomputing centers, enabling secure scientific workflows on infrastructure organizations control.</li>
	<li>Leading global research institutions, including the U.S. Department of Energy&rsquo;s Argonne National Laboratory, are using Nemotron to build agents to speed scientific discovery.</li>
</ul>

<p>NVIDIA today introduced NVIDIA Nemotron for Science, bringing together scientific applications of its <a href="https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-powers-specialized-agents-with-multimodal-reasoning/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>NVIDIA Nemotron&trade; 3.5 Super VL</u></a> open model, a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes to help researchers build specialized agents for scientific discovery.</p>

<p>Built on Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Nemotron for Science helps researchers develop agents that reason through scientific problems and put specialized research tools to work. With post-training, scientists can adapt the model to specialized tasks such as conducting experiments for chemistry, protein design and more.</p>

<p>Part of Nemotron for Science, <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-litmus-bench-v0.2/tree/cf18cb1b2392d04a2ac578637462261d62da11d7" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>LitmusBench v0.2</u></a> is a new open dataset with nearly 50,000 questions for training and evaluating language models on chemistry reasoning. Drawing on molecular properties and experimental drug discovery data, it helps researchers improve models&rsquo; ability to predict how molecules behave, including their solubility and how the human body processes them.</p>

<p>Life sciences companies Lila Sciences, Terray Therapeutics and Therna are using and customizing NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for science applications. Use cases include extracting chemical knowledge, planning experiments and designing therapeutics and laboratory protocols. Major research centers like Argonne and J&uuml;lich Supercomputing Centre are integrating it into their drug and scientific discovery AI agents.</p>

<p>&ldquo;Accelerated computing is transforming how scientists tackle the world&rsquo;s most complex challenges,&rdquo; said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. &ldquo;Nemotron for Science gives researchers open models, scientific data and post-training recipes to build specialized agents that reason through scientific problems and use CUDA-X accelerated tools to turn ideas into discoveries.&rdquo;</p>

<p><strong>Post-Training Nemotron Open Models for Scientific Discovery</strong><br />
Researchers can post-train Nemotron open models with domain-specific data to improve performance on specialized scientific tasks. They can integrate the resulting model into agent workflows that interpret scientific information, generate code and call computational tools. These workflows can use <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/technologies/cuda-x/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>NVIDIA CUDA-X</u></a>&trade; accelerated tools to perform scientific computation.</p>

<p><strong>Terray Therapeutics</strong> post-trained Nemotron to extract reactants, products and reaction conditions from scientific diagrams, surpassing previously published results on two benchmarks. On the RxnScribe test, it recovered about 76% of annotated reactions under the benchmark&rsquo;s matching criteria, helping turn published chemistry discoveries into structured data for synthesis planning and scientific agents.</p>

<p><strong>Lila Sciences</strong> used Nemotron to design execution-ready laboratory protocols for its automated labs, matching frontier-level performance without requiring additional fine-tuning. Post-training with laboratory feedback nearly doubled the model&rsquo;s accuracy for making quantum dots &mdash; nanoscale crystals used in screens and solar panels &mdash; to 61%, exceeding GPT-6 Astra&rsquo;s 54% at 10-20x lower inference cost. These gains help agents and materials scientists translate desired material properties into synthesis recipes, advancing the discovery of new materials.</p>

<p><strong>Therna</strong> collaborated with NVIDIA to post-train Nemotron for agentic mRNA therapeutic design, nearly doubling accuracy in predicting protein-expression ranges over frontier models. Scientists preferred its explanations over those from the base model in 96% of comparisons. These gains could help scientists tailor mRNA designs for the desired protein production in specific cell types as they scale to human use.</p>

<p><strong>Researchers Speed Science With Nemotron Models and Datasets</strong><br />
Leading research institutions are using NVIDIA Nemotron models and datasets to advance scientific discovery at every scale, from individual researchers&rsquo; desktops to labs and supercomputing centers.</p>

<p>By helping researchers rapidly design and evaluate novel molecules across the periodic table, the work has the potential to open new pathways for applications in critical materials and minerals, national security and cancer treatment.</p>

<p>Argonne is integrating Nemotron into its StructBioReasoner multi-agent system to design and evaluate protein-based therapeutic candidates for treatment of cancer and other diseases.</p>

<p>KTH Royal Institute of Technology has built an AI agent on Nemotron that repairs broken GROMACS molecular dynamics setups on its own. In one overnight run on a single <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-spark/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>NVIDIA DGX Spark</u></a>&trade; system, the agent fixed 81% of test cases with reasoning enabled, and every fix was checked independently by GROMACS itself.</p>

<p>RIKEN has made NVIDIA Nemotron, including Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, available on its RIKYU AI supercomputing platform through RiVault, its inference gateway, enabling researchers to access the models for scientific research and the development of accelerated applications.</p>

<p><strong>Availability</strong><br />
<a href="https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL</u></a> and the <a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-litmus-bench-v0.2/tree/cf18cb1b2392d04a2ac578637462261d62da11d7" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>LitmusBench v0.2</u></a> chemistry dataset are available now on Hugging Face. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model was also optimized to run locally on a 128GB <a href="https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/products/workstations/dgx-spark/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><u>NVIDIA DGX Spark system</u></a>.</p>

<p><em>Learn more in this </em><a href="https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/post-training-nvidia-nemotron-to-increase-accuracy-in-your-scientific-domain/" rel="nofollow" target="_blank" title=""><em><u>technical blog</u></em></a><em> on post-training NVIDIA Nemotron to increase accuracy across scientific domains. </em></p>
